newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hoechst makes buyout offer for Roussel.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst makes buyout offer for Roussel.

text.p: Germany chemicals conglomerate Hoechst AG, which holds 56.53 percent of Roussel Uclaf, announced on Wednesay an 18.1 billion franc ($3.5 billion) offer to buy out minority shareholders of the French pharmaceuticals group.

"This operation is the logical and natural extension of the close cooperation between the Hoechst group and Roussel Uclaf which began in 1968 with agreements in research and development and the taking of a first minority stake in Roussel Uclaf," Hoechst said in a statement.
Hoechst valued the transaction to take full control of Roussel Uclaf at 18.1 billion francs.
The operation will be one of the biggest announced this year on the Paris bourse and continues the worldwide consolidation that is reshaping the pharmaceutical industry.

The bid offers minority shareholders a 12 percent premium on the average price of the common stock over the previous month and 19 percent over the average price over the previous three months, Hoechst said.
Hoechst priced the offer at 1,530 francs per ordinary share and 1,330 francs per preference share.
Hoechst said the move would boost its industrial strength in three strategic regions -- Germany, France and the United States.
Industry analysts had been expecting Hoechst to bid for full control of Roussel Uclaf as part of a move to seek a separate stock market quotation for Hoechst Marion Roussel, its drug division.
The buyout offer is the second major transaction announced by Hoechst in two days.
On Tuesday, the company announced it would merge its speciality chemicals business with Swiss group Clariant AG in a bid to overcome difficult conditions in the sector.
The supervisory board of Hoechst AG, Societe Francaise Hoechst and Roussel Uclaf, approved the offer terms on Tuesday.
The first day of the public offer and the requotation of Roussel stock is on December 20, Hoechst said.

French state holding company ERAP, the second largest shareholder in Roussel after Hoechst with 4.28 percent of Roussel's capital, has already indicated it will tender its shares in the offer, Hoechst said. ($ = 5.223 French Francs)
